title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers
section: Volumes of Solids of Revolution ▷ Disks and washers
terms: solid of revolution; disk method; washer method; outer radius; inner radius; cross- sectional area.

exposition.text:
Rotating a region about an axis creates a solid of revolution. A slice perpendicular to the axis
2 2 2
yields a disk of area πR or a washer of area π(R − r ), where radii are distances from the axis.
R
Integrate this cross-sectional area along the axis: V = A(s)ds. Rotating about a horizontal
axis usually suggests vertical slices and dx; a vertical axis suggests horizontal slices and dy.
For shifted axes subtract the axis coordinate before squaring. If the region crosses the axis, ro-
tating separate signed sides can overlap, so identify the actual cross-section. A change in which
boundary is farthest from the axis requires a split. Distinguish the square of the difference from
the difference of squares: washers use the latter.
